questions.prompt: How do |+> and |-> compare under direct Z measurement?

options.text: Their probabilities depend on their global phases

questions.explanation: Their amplitudes differ by a relative sign, but their squared magnitudes agree. A different measurement basis can distinguish them.

questions.prompt: Which change is only a global phase?
questions.explanation: The factor i has magnitude one and affects all amplitudes equally. It leaves all physical measurement predictions unchanged.

questions.prompt: When two paths interfere, what is added before computing a probability?
questions.explanation: Interference combines signed or complex contributions to the same outcome. Squaring first would discard the phase information needed for cancellation.

questions.prompt: Starting from |0>, what is the output of H followed by H?
questions.explanation: The first H prepares |+>, and the second maps it back to |0>. The contributions to |1> cancel.

questions.prompt: Starting from |0>, what is the output of H, then Z, then H?

options.text: An equal classical mixture of 0 and 1

questions.explanation: The intermediate states are |+> and |->. The final H maps |-> to |1>.

questions.prompt: For (|0>+exp(i phi)|1>)/sqrt(2), what is P(0) after H when phi=pi/2?
questions.explanation: Insert cos(pi/2)=0 into P(0)=(1+cos(phi))/2. This phase gives equal output probabilities.

questions.prompt: Two contributions to the same output amplitude are 1/2 and -1/2. What probability results?
questions.explanation: The amplitudes sum to zero before taking the squared magnitude. Adding their individual probabilities would incorrectly omit interference.

questions.prompt: A source prepares |0> or |1> with equal classical probability. What happens if H precedes Z measurement?

options.text: The two preparation probabilities interfere destructively

questions.explanation: H maps the two preparations to |+> and |->, each with 50/50 Z outcomes. A classical mixture has no relative phase connecting its alternatives.

questions.prompt: Which experiment distinguishes |+> from |-> in one ideal shot?

options.text: Apply H, then measure in Z
Multiply both amplitudes by -1, then measure in Z
Repeat direct Z measurement on the same collapsed state

questions.explanation: H maps these orthogonal states to |0> and |1>. The other listed operations do not convert the original relative-sign difference into distinct outcomes.

questions.prompt: In the phase experiment, P(0) after H is 3/4. What follows about phi?

options.text: cos(phi)=1/2, but phi is not uniquely determined
The input Z probabilities were 3/4 and 1/4
The input had no relative phase

questions.explanation: Solving 3/4=(1+cos(phi))/2 gives cos(phi)=1/2. For example, pi/3 and -pi/3 give the same result.
